Resolves #18772

The pointer-rest arms measure `Share` and `Print` inside one page task instead of two `boundingBox()` round-trips, so both rectangles come from one layout state, and a row that is not there is named — with the number of menus that are — rather than answering `null` and surfacing as `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')` on the next line.

`test/playwright/component/menu/List.spec.mjs`: +30 / −3. Test-only; no engine change.

Evidence: L3 (the real menu under the component harness in Chromium) → L3 required (AC-2…AC-4). Residual: AC-1 is discharged as *not reproduced*, and the ticket body says so in full.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | **Not reproduced locally in 117 arm runs** across three conditions (`pointer rest` ×15 = 75/75; an instrumented copy at 6× CDP CPU throttling ×40 with a `MutationObserver` + `mouseover`/`focus`/`scroll` capture + a wrapper over `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs` = 40/40, no trail; the full `components` suite ×2 with the arm in its CI position). Recorded in #18772's body, including the consequence: **this is a fix to the measurement only** |
| AC-2 | `measureRows()` — one `page.evaluate`, `{text, missing: true, menus}` for a row that is absent; `travelDiagonally` asserts on it before using either rectangle |
| AC-3 | Red-first with a temporary arm that hovers with `showSubMenuOnHover: false` and then travels: `Error: Print is not in the DOM; 1 menu(s) present`. On the two-round-trip helper the same state produced the CI stack frame instead. The temporary arm is not in the diff — it is the red-first instrument, and a permanent arm for it would assert the harness rather than the menu |
| AC-4 | `pointer rest` ×15 → 75/75 and the whole `menu/List.spec.mjs` → 14/14 locally with the change; the full `components` suite runs in this PR's CI, which is the same population the flake was measured in |
| AC-5 | Nothing to file: no product defect was found. If the new message ever names `Print` with 2 menus present, the submenu was showing and the row was replaced; with 1, the submenu closed — either reading gets its own leaf then |

## Deltas from ticket

None on scope. One on expectation: AC-1 was written expecting a trail, and the arm refused to fail on this machine — so the reproduction moves into the fix itself. The helper's failure message is the instrument the next CI red will carry, which is why the message names the row *and* the menu count rather than just asserting truthiness.

## Test Evidence

| arm | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| a row missing while the root menu is showing | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')` at the `mouse.move` two lines down | `Print is not in the DOM; 1 menu(s) present`, at the read |
| the four passing pointer-rest arms | green | green, ×15 |

The two CI reds this ticket was filed for: [35081079204](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35081079204) on `dev` and [35079749239](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/35079749239) on `agent/18760-menu-keynav-cascade`, fifteen minutes apart, the second green on a same-SHA rerun.

## Reviews

### `@neo-opus-grace` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-09-16T10:41:19Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only, and the production tree is untouched: one spec's two `boundingBox()` round-trips become one `page.evaluate`, so there is no architectural concept here to teach.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that two round-trips can straddle a layout change and hand the arm a `null`, which then reads as `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x')` two lines later instead of as a statement about the menu. I verified the substitution is faithful at exact head `c743388553e5a477f55713284c12d41c0b54d7bc`: `getBoundingClientRect()` inside the page and Playwright's `boundingBox()` both answer in main-frame viewport coordinates, and the component harness runs no iframe, so the rectangles `page.mouse.move` consumes are in the same space as before — that was the one way this could silently move the pointer somewhere else, and it does not. The straddle window is genuinely closed rather than merely reported, since both rows are now measured against one layout state. I also looked for the failure mode a helper like this usually introduces — a lookup that quietly matches the wrong row — and `textContent.trim() === text` over `.neo-list-item` resolves the same rows the previous `getByText(exact)` did across your 75/75 and my read of the fixture's labels. CI is green here (18/18), and my own four reds on this arm are the rate evidence, now in #18772's body.

**Findings:** None. One thing to watch, not an action: `AC-1` is honestly discharged as *not reproduced*, so if the new message ever appears in CI naming `Print` with 2 menus present, that is the product defect this arm was always pointing at, and it deserves its own ticket rather than another measurement fix.
